title: Data-integrity audit of the CP-AnemiC conjunctival anaemia dataset: code, duplicate maps and results
description: Code, duplicate maps and out-of-fold predictions for the article Class-conditional duplicate images inflate the reported performance of conjunctival anaemia detection in children: a data-integrity audit of the CP-AnemiC dataset. The four-stage duplicate audit (SHA-256, perceptual hashing with mirror and rotations, exhaustive SIFT + RANSAC search with photometric verification) finds about 338 distinct images among the 710 rows of CP-AnemiC version 1, with duplicates confined to one anaemia class. This is not a new benchmark: CP-AnemiC has been withdrawn by its authors and its images cannot be downloaded from Mendeley Data any more; the images and the per-child clinical metadata are not redistributed here. Includes colour-feature classifiers with nested repeated cross-validation, CNNs (PyTorch), cluster-aware statistics, explainability, sensitivity analyses and the validation of the duplicate detector.

creators.name: Arce Apaza, Bisleyn de la Flor

notes: The CP-AnemiC images are not redistributed here; download them from Mendeley Data (CC BY 4.0). meta_groups.csv and the result tables are derived from CP-AnemiC and released under CC BY 4.0; the code is MIT.
